arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ms. Blatt argued that general laws do not reach foreign sovereigns in criminal cases.
Ms. Blatt stated that Congress has not authorized courts to convict foreign nations.
Mr. Feigin argued that the statute recognizes potential implications for other cases.
Mr. Feigin contended that the law ensures proper handling of these situations.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The dispute centers on whether a general federal statute grants courts power to prosecute a foreign sovereign. The bank claims the law lacks a clear statement of intent to waive immunity. The government argues the statute provides sufficient authority for criminal prosecution.
